How a personal injury case works
From claim to courtroom, step by step
We investigate, gather the evidence and medical records, and open your claim with every insurer responsible for your injuries.
We present a detailed demand for all of your damages and negotiate hard with the insurance company for a fair settlement.
If the insurer won’t be fair, we file a lawsuit. Discovery, depositions and expert testimony build your case for court.

I’m Jennifer Cabrera-Torres, Founder & Managing Attorney of Cabrera Torres Law Firm. Before becoming an attorney, I spent more than 15 years as a personal injury trial paralegal, developing a deep understanding of the preparation, persistence, and personal attention injury cases require.

Born in Atlanta and raised in Gwinnett County by immigrant parents, I’m proud to serve the community I’ve long called home. Establishing my firm in Norcross is especially meaningful because it allows me to advocate for individuals and families in the community that helped shape who I am.
As the first in my family to graduate from college and law school, my journey has been shaped by profound loss, meaningful new beginnings, and a determination to keep moving forward.

Three days after graduating from college, I lost my father. What should have been a time of celebration became a season of grief as I prepared for the LSAT and pursued my goal of becoming an attorney. That experience taught me how suddenly life can change—and how much it matters to have someone beside you during difficult moments.

Years later, during the COVID-19 pandemic, I completed my law school final exams at 40 weeks pregnant and welcomed my first child the following day. Becoming a mother while pursuing my legal education strengthened my resolve and deepened my appreciation for the families who depend on the work I do.

Those experiences shape how I represent people whose lives have been disrupted by an injury. I understand that your case involves more than medical records and insurance claims. It can affect your livelihood, your family, your independence, and your sense of security.

I represent clients in personal injury matters involving car accidents, tractor-trailer collisions, wrongful death, dog bites, and slip-and-fall incidents. I bring litigation experience, careful preparation, and a personal commitment to helping you understand your options and make informed decisions throughout your case.
Fluent in English and Spanish, I want you to feel heard, understand the process, and know who is standing beside you.

When someone else’s carelessness causes an injury, Georgia law lets you demand financial accountability. Here is what we handle and how a claim works.

Crashes are the most common cause of serious injury in Georgia. We investigate fault, deal with the insurers so you don’t have to, and pursue every available policy, including your own underinsured coverage.

A collision with an 18-wheeler or commercial truck can be catastrophic. These cases involve federal safety rules, trucking companies and their insurers, and evidence like driver logs and black-box data that has to be secured fast.

Georgia holds owners responsible when they knew their dog was dangerous or let it run loose in violation of a local leash ordinance. Bites often mean scarring, infection and lasting trauma, especially for children.
Property owners must keep their premises reasonably safe. When a wet floor, broken stair or poor lighting causes a fall, the business’s commercial liability insurance is where the claim goes.
When an injury changes a life or ends one, the claim has to account for the whole future: lifetime care, lost income, and the full value of a life.

Almost always an insurance company: the at-fault driver’s policy, a business’s commercial liability coverage after a fall, or a dog owner’s homeowner’s policy. We examine every available policy, including your own uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage.

A selection of recent settlements and verdicts in car, truck, slip-and-fall, products liability and serious-injury cases across metro Atlanta.

A commercial truck struck our client, causing a shoulder injury that required surgery. We recovered $1.2 million from the trucking company for medical costs, pain and suffering, and the long-term impact on his ability to work.

A tractor-trailer turned unlawfully into our client’s lane at a Gwinnett County intersection. Strategic litigation and mediation produced a $550,000 settlement against the trucking company and its insurer.
A highway rear-end collision left our client with debilitating neck pain and spinal damage requiring cervical disc replacement. We secured $500,000 for his recovery and lost income.
A driver who failed to yield while turning left caused significant back and knee injuries, including an ACL tear. We recovered $495,000 for medical bills, physical limitations and hardship.
In a multi-vehicle crash, our client sustained herniated discs in his neck and lower back and underwent spine surgery. We recovered $490,000 for treatment and lasting effects.
A head-on crash caused by a drunk driver resulted in catastrophic spine injuries and a 65% permanent impairment rating. We obtained $425,000 for lost income and quality of life.
Another driver failed to yield while turning across traffic, totaling our client’s vehicle and causing serious spinal injuries. After months of treatment, we secured $277,908.
Our client slipped and fell at a major national retail chain, suffering injuries that required surgery and future treatment. We secured a $275,000 settlement.
Faulty plumbing at a leading international hotel chain caused our client’s fall and injuries. We secured a $250,000 settlement.
After being struck by a drunk driver who fled the scene, our client was left with chronic pain and disc herniations. Despite policy limits, we secured $245,000 by pursuing all available coverage.

A products liability case against a leading global manufacturer of industrial equipment, for an injury that required surgery and significant future medical treatment. We secured a $230,000 settlement.

Nothing up front. We work on a contingency fee, which means we are paid a percentage only if we recover money for you. The initial consultation is free.
Generally two years from the date of injury for most personal injury cases. Exceptions can shorten or extend that deadline, so it is important to call early.
Current and future medical expenses, lost wages, reduced earning capacity, out-of-pocket costs, pain and suffering, and in some cases compensation for scarring or diminished quality of life.
Almost always an insurance company: the at-fault driver’s policy, a business’s commercial liability coverage, or a homeowner’s policy. We examine every available policy, including your own.
The large majority of cases resolve by settlement. We prepare every case as if it will be tried because that produces better offers, and we are ready to go to court when it is needed.
Get medical care, call the police, photograph the scene and the vehicles, collect witness information, and do not give a recorded statement to the other side’s insurer before speaking with a lawyer.
You are not required to. Adjusters are looking for statements that lower the value of your claim. Let us handle those conversations.
Georgia follows modified comparative negligence: you can recover as long as you are less than 50% at fault, and your compensation is reduced by your share of the blame.
Your own uninsured or underinsured motorist (UM/UIM) coverage may pay your damages. We review every available policy to find coverage.
